blocks.title: Standard enthalpy change of formation
blocks.text: The standard enthalpy change of formation of a compound, delta Hf, is the enthalpy change when one mole of the compound is formed from its elements under standard conditions. It can be exothermic or endothermic.
For methane, C(s) + 2H2(g) gives CH4(g), delta Hf = -74.8 kJ per mol.

blocks.prompt: Which equation represents the standard enthalpy of formation of C2H4: 2C(diamond) + 2H2 giving C2H4, or 2C(graphite) + 2H2 giving C2H4?
blocks.explanation: The graphite equation: formation is defined from the elements in their standard states, and the standard state of carbon is graphite, not diamond, with one mole of the compound formed.

items: Delta Hf: one mole of compound from its elements in their standard states; may be exothermic or endothermic (methane -74.8 kJ per mol).
